reproduction_target: A single-nucleus RNA-seq + Xenium spatial-transcriptomics cell atlas of healthy human Achilles tendon across four microanatomical zones (enthesis, midbody, myotendinous junction, adjacent triceps surae muscle) from surgical amputation donors. The wet-lab half generates the data (tissue collection, nuclei isolation with a published CST-buffer protocol, 10X Chromium Next GEM 3' v3.1 libraries, NovaSeq 6000 sequencing, Xenium in-situ with a 300-gene Human Multi Tissue and Cancer panel plus a bespoke 101-gene add-on panel, post-Xenium H&E). The computational target is the analysis chain that produces every figure and every biological claim: scflow quantnuclei (FastQC v0.12.1, kb_python kb count v0.27.3 against Ensembl GRCh38 release 106, kmer 31, spliced+unspliced merge) -> per-sample QC filtering -> ambient-RNA correction (celda decontX v1.14.0, SoupX v1.6.2) and doublet removal (scDblFinder v1.12.0) -> Seurat v4.3.0.1 merge/log-normalise/5000 HVG/50 PC -> a custom Seurat-to-AnnData conversion script -> scvi-tools v1.0.2 integration with Ray autotune hyperparameter search and 60 training epochs -> Louvain clustering on 40 scVI PCs with clustree v0.5.0 and LISI v1.0 -> marker-based broad and fine annotation (with Harmony v1.2.0 rescuing the muscle subset) -> MiloR v1.10.0 differential abundance -> pseudobulk DESeq2 v1.40.2 LRT on '~ patient + microanatomical_site' -> DEGreport v1.36.0 and clusterProfiler v4.10.0 GO:BP enrichment -> SCENIC regulon inference -> Liana v0.1.14 / CellPhoneDB ligand-receptor with CrossTalkeR v1.4.0 -> and, for the spatial half, 10X Xenium Onboard Analysis followed by Seurat v5.3.0 (R v4.5.1) filtering, Harmony IntegrateLayers, SCTransform, PCA/UMAP and FindTransferAnchors/TransferData label transfer from the snRNA-seq reference. Neither the sequencing data nor the analysis code is available at the time of this assessment: both are promised in the future tense.
granularity_note: 27 computational steps and 7 wet-lab steps derived from the 'MATERIALS AND METHODS' prose of the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML, one step per named tool or analysis invocation, per guide Step 1 (prose fallback). No workflow file, script or notebook exists to read: the paper links no repository of its own. The two GitHub URLs that do appear in Methods (github.com/cribbslab/scflow and github.com/mamba-org/mamba) are citations of third-party TOOLS the authors used, not deposits of this paper's analysis code, and neither was opened beyond noting its presence in the text. Step C19 (SCENIC) is enumerated even though it appears only in Results and has no Methods paragraph at all, because it produces a figure panel (Figure S5N) and a stated biological conclusion.

steps.label: Raw NGS quality control and mapping orchestrated by the 'scflow quantnuclei' pipeline (cited as https://github.com/cribbslab/scflow; python v3.8.15). No scflow version, release tag or commit SHA is given, and no pipeline configuration/YAML is deposited, so the orchestration layer is a moving default-branch reference
Quality control of FASTQ files with FastQC (v0.12.1) inside the scflow quantnuclei pipeline; no parameters or cutoffs stated and no QC report deposited

Map FASTQ files to the human Ensembl GRCh38 transcriptome (release 106) with kb_python 'kb count' (v0.27.3), kmer size = 31; spliced and unspliced matrices merged into the downstream count matrix. Reference release is pinned but the raw reads are not available

Per-sample cell-level quality filtering in R (v4.4.1) / RStudio Server (v2024.09.0 build 375) with SingleCellExperiment (v1.24.0) and Seurat (v4.3.0.1): 'poor quality cells were removed by filtering on a per-sample basis for low number of cells and features and high mitochondrial ratio'. No per-sample thresholds are reported anywhere in the manuscript or supplement

Ambient-RNA detection with the decontX function of celda (v1.14.0); droplets with decontX score > 0.3 removed and genes with >2% ambient contamination removed (8 genes; the 8 gene names are not listed)
Doublet calling and removal with scDblFinder (v1.12.0); no parameters, no expected-doublet-rate and no random seed are stated for a stochastic method

Second ambient-RNA round with SoupX (v1.6.2) 'using parameters customised to each sample'; droplets with >30% SoupX contamination removed and the SoupX-adjusted count matrix carried downstream. The per-sample custom parameters are stated to exist but are not reported
Merge all datasets in Seurat (v4.3.0.1), log-normalise, select 5,000 variable features, scale the data and compute 50 principal components

Convert the Seurat object to AnnData format: 'A custom script was used to convert the Seurat object to Anndata format'. The script is not deposited, not linked and not described; the anndata version is given only as an RRID (SCR_018209) with no version number

Batch integration across patient and sequencing batch with scvi-tools (v1.0.2) in Jupyter Notebook (v7.2.1): Ray autotune was used to select optimal hyperparameters, which were then used in the scVI model; the model was trained with vae.train for 60 epochs and the latent embeddings returned to the Seurat object. The autotune search space and the selected hyperparameters are not reported, no random seed is given, and scVI is a stochastic neural method

Neighbour graph construction, Louvain clustering and dimensionality reduction in Seurat on the scVI embeddings using 40 PCs; integration success assessed with elbow plots and LISI scores (LISI v1.0); clustree (v0.5.0) used to assess optimal clustering resolution. The resolution value actually chosen is never stated

Marker-gene calculation with Seurat FindAllMarkers() and visualisation with Seurat DoHeatmap(), Seurat DotPlot(), scDotPlot (v1.1.0) and SCpubr (v2.0.2). No test, logFC threshold, min.pct or adjusted-p cutoff is stated for FindAllMarkers()

Fine annotation: subset each broad cell type (fibroblasts, muscle, immune, non-fibroblast stromal) and re-cluster with the C8-C11 procedure but 2,000 variable genes; the muscle subset failed scVI integration QC (clusters >80% from one patient) and was reintegrated with Harmony (v1.2.0). 'In some cases, smaller clusters were merged if they did not express biologically meaningful distinct marker genes' - a manual, unrecorded curation step
Differential abundance of broad cell types and of fibroblast subsets across microanatomy with MiloR (v1.10.0); no k, d, prop, refinement scheme or SpatialFDR threshold is stated

Pseudobulk differential gene expression: aggregate per cell type with Seurat AggregateExpression(), drop genes with fewer than 10 reads, then DESeq2 (v1.40.2) with design formula '~ patient + microanatomical_site' and the likelihood ratio test; comparisons drawn only where cells from at least three donors were present at each microanatomy. No significance threshold is stated
Clustering and visualisation of the differentially expressed genes with DEGreport (v1.36.0); no parameters stated

GO:BP over-representation with clusterProfiler (v4.10.0) on the gene clusters grouped into 'enthesis-high', 'muscle-high' and 'tendon-high' classes, using a custom background of all genes expressed in that cell type, plotted with ggplot2 (no version given). The mapping from DEGreport clusters to the three classes, the p/q cutoffs, and the GO annotation database version (org.Hs.eg.db / GO release) are all unstated
Per-fibroblast-subtype pathway enrichment: pseudobulk-aggregate expression per subtype and pass the top 200 genes by count number to clusterProfiler (v4.10.0)

SCENIC regulon inference producing the fibroblast-subset transcriptional networks of Figure S5N and the IRF3 / MYF6 / SOX9 regulon claims in the text. This analysis appears ONLY in Results ('We performed SCENIC analysis (24)'), citing the SCENIC+ paper; there is no Methods paragraph, no software version, no motif/cisTarget database version, no parameters and no random seed

Ligand-receptor inference between finely annotated cell types at each microanatomy with Liana (v0.1.14) using the CellPhoneDB resource, selecting interactions with 'a p-value of at least 0.05'. The CellPhoneDB database version bundled with Liana is not stated, nor is the aggregation method or permutation count
Visualisation of the ligand-receptor results with CrossTalkeR (v1.4.0) plot_cci() and Liana liana_dotplot(); no parameters stated

Primary processing of the Xenium run with the 10X Genomics Xenium Onboard Analysis (RRID SCR_026158) - closed instrument software with no version, no analysis-bundle identifier and no segmentation settings reported; the Xenium Analyzer User Guide is cited as CG000584 Rev J

Xenium output filtering in Seurat (v5.3.0) under R (v4.5.1) and RStudio Server Pro build 467.pro1: 'Filtering was performed according to cell size, number of transcripts and number of probes'. No thresholds are given for any of the three criteria

Integration of the four Xenium tissue pieces with Harmony via Seurat IntegrateLayers(); no Harmony version is restated in the spatial section (v1.2.0 appears only in the snRNA-seq section) and no integration parameters are given

Normalisation of the Xenium data with SCTransform followed by the standard Seurat dimensionality-reduction workflow, RunPCA() and RunUMAP(); no number of dimensions, no variable-feature count and no UMAP parameters are stated

Transfer of broad and fine annotation labels from the snRNA-seq reference onto the Xenium data with Seurat FindTransferAnchors() and TransferData(); no reduction, no dims, no k.weight and no prediction-score cutoff are stated. This step depends on the snRNA-seq object produced by C1-C13, which is itself not deposited

Subset the broad spatial cell types (immune, fibroblast, muscle, stromal) and repeat C24-C26 to define fine cell types; upload annotations to 10x Genomics Xenium Explorer with post-Xenium H&E to generate figures; SCpubr (v2.0.2) used for UMAP plots. Xenium Explorer carries no version

Wet-lab: Achilles tendon and adjacent triceps surae collection from above-knee amputation donors (sarcoma), dissection into 1 cm strips from enthesis to MTJ, photography for topographical reference, snap-freezing in liquid nitrogen and storage at -80 C; formalin fixation of parallel pieces. Ethics: Oxford Musculoskeletal Biobank 19/SC/0134

Wet-lab: H&E histology of paraffin-embedded Achilles samples (5 um sections, Gill's III Haematoxylin 8 min, 0.1% sodium bicarbonate 30 s, 0.3% acid alcohol 30 s, 0.5% aqueous Eosin Y 5 min, DPX mount) imaged on a MoticEasyScan One slide scanner

Wet-lab: nuclei isolation from snap-frozen tissue with the authors' published CST-buffer protocol (NaCl/Tris-HCl pH 7.5/CaCl2/MgCl2 with CHAPS, BSA, RNase and protease inhibitors), 10 min rotation at 4 C, 40 um strainer, 500 g 5 min at 4 C, DAPI haemocytometer counting

Wet-lab: snRNA-seq library preparation and sequencing - nuclei diluted to 860-1,000 nuclei/ul, 10X Chromium Controller, Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 3' Reagent Kits v3.1, Single Index Kit T Set A, QC on Agilent 4150 TapeStation, sequencing on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 at a minimum of ~20,000 read pairs per expected nucleus (Azenta Life Sciences)

Wet-lab: Xenium sample preparation - H&E-guided ROI selection, tissue-array embedding at 10.45 mm x 22.45 mm, 5 um sections onto Xenium slides (PN-3000941) per 10X CG000578 Rev E, 45 C bake for 3 h, desiccator storage

Wet-lab: Xenium in-situ run - deparaffinisation/decrosslinking per 10X CG000580 Rev E, hybridisation per CG000749 Rev B with the Xenium Human Multi Tissue and Cancer Probe Panel (300 genes) plus a bespoke Add-On Custom Probe Panel of 101 genes (gene list in Data S3), cell segmentation staining and Xenium Analyzer run per CG000584 Rev J
Wet-lab: post-Xenium H&E staining per 10X CG000613 Rev A, DPX coverslipping and imaging on the MoticEasyScan One slide scanner

headline.static_readiness: 0/27 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification); unexecuted, and in this case there is no declared environment to validate at all
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI on all 27 computational steps; 0 RI. This is a floor result, and the cause is a single sentence in the back matter rather than a scatter of small omissions. The paper's entire availability statement reads: 'All the code used for the data analysis of this paper will be made available on GitHub. All the transcriptomics data in this manuscript will be made available upon publication.' Both promises are in the future tense; neither carries a URL, a repository name, an accession, a DOI or an embargo date. There is therefore no code artifact and no data artifact in existence as of this assessment, which zeroes the data and code axes on every computational step and caps the whole paper at NI regardless of how well the methods are written. And they are written well: this is one of the more carefully versioned Methods sections in the sample. Twenty-two distinct packages carry exact version strings (FastQC v0.12.1, kb_python v0.27.3, R v4.4.1, SingleCellExperiment v1.24.0, Seurat v4.3.0.1 for snRNA-seq and v5.3.0 under R v4.5.1 for spatial, celda v1.14.0, scDblFinder v1.12.0, SoupX v1.6.2, scvi-tools v1.0.2, Jupyter v7.2.1, LISI v1.0, clustree v0.5.0, scDotPlot v1.1.0, SCpubr v2.0.2, Harmony v1.2.0, MiloR v1.10.0, DESeq2 v1.40.2, DEGreport v1.36.0, clusterProfiler v4.10.0, Liana v0.1.14, CrossTalkeR v1.4.0, python v3.8.15), the transcriptome reference is pinned to Ensembl GRCh38 release 106, and the DESeq2 design formula is given verbatim. The authors even name mamba v1.4.4 'for version control' - but no environment file, lockfile or container is claimed to be shipped anywhere, so this is a statement about the authors' own practice, not a distributable artifact. That is why capture_claim is exact_pins_partial and not env_lock_claimed. The second-order weakness, which would still bite after the data and code appear, is that the numeric thresholds of the subjective steps are systematically missing: the per-sample QC cutoffs (C4), the SoupX per-sample custom parameters (C7, explicitly stated to exist but not reported), the chosen Louvain resolution (C11), the FindAllMarkers test and cutoffs (C12), the MiloR neighbourhood parameters (C14), the DESeq2 significance threshold (C15), the clusterProfiler cutoffs and GO release (C17), and every Xenium filtering threshold (C23) and label-transfer parameter (C26). Three steps are structurally unrecoverable from prose alone even with perfect data: the 'custom script' that converts Seurat to AnnData (C9) is neither deposited nor described; the SCENIC regulon analysis (C19) that supports the IRF3/MYF6/SOX9 claims has no Methods paragraph, no version and no motif-database release; and the Xenium Onboard Analysis (C22) is closed instrument software with no version recorded. Four stochastic steps (scDblFinder, scVI with Ray-autotuned hyperparameters trained 60 epochs, SCENIC, Liana permutation testing) report no random seed, so even a perfect artifact release would land at distributional agreement rather than bit-identity. Upper bound if and only if the promised GitHub repository and the promised data deposit both materialise with the versions already stated in prose: roughly RI on the ~22 steps that already carry exact pins, with C1 (unpinned scflow), C9 (custom script), C19 (SCENIC) and C22 (Xenium Onboard) remaining NI unless separately documented. Stage-2 has nothing to check today: there is no repository to open.
headline.coverage: 27 computational steps and 7 wet-lab steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS 'MATERIALS AND METHODS' (Ethics; Tissue acquisition and processing; H&E imaging; Single nucleus RNA sequencing - Nuclei isolation, Library preparation and sequencing; Single nucleus RNA sequencing data analysis - Quality control and filtering, Data integration clustering and broad annotation, Fine annotation, Differential abundance of cell types across microanatomy, Differential gene expression and pathway enrichment, Ligand-receptor interactions; Spatial transcriptomics - Sample preparation and 10X Xenium, Post-Xenium H&E staining, Spatial transcriptomics data analysis) plus the SCENIC analysis reported only in Results. Coverage = 34/34 (100%) of enumerated steps; the computational denominator is S = 27 and wet-lab W = 7 (scored OOS, not failed).

gaps.where: C1-C27 (every computational step; the paper as a whole)
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked. The complete code statement is, verbatim: 'All the code used for the data analysis of this paper will be made available on GitHub.' Future tense, no organisation, no repository name, no URL, no DOI, no commit, no release, no date. The two GitHub links that do appear in Methods (https://github.com/cribbslab/scflow and https://github.com/mamba-org/mamba) are citations of third-party tools, not deposits of this paper's code, and the scflow link carries no version or commit either. As a result the code axis is 0 on all 27 computational steps, and the steps whose behaviour lives entirely in unpublished code - C4 QC thresholds, C7 SoupX per-sample parameters, C9 the Seurat-to-AnnData converter, C13 the manual cluster merges - have no recovery path other than contacting the authors.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the analysis repository now (bioRxiv preprints can carry a live link), archive a tagged release with a Zenodo DOI, and cite that DOI in the manuscript rather than a future-tense promise. Map each Methods subsection to the script or notebook that implements it.

gaps.where: C1-C27 (all computational steps; the snRNA-seq FASTQ, the count matrices, the annotated objects and the Xenium outputs)
gaps.missing: No data accession of any kind appears anywhere in the manuscript. The complete data statement is, verbatim: 'All the transcriptomics data in this manuscript will be made available upon publication.' There is no GEO series, no ArrayExpress/BioStudies identifier, no SRA/ENA project, no EGA/dbGaP study for what is human patient-derived sequence data, no figshare or Zenodo deposit, no cellxgene or CZI Tendon Seed Network portal link, and no statement of whether access will be open or controlled. Donor metadata (age, sex, affected side, de-identified study ID) is given in Table 1, so the sample-to-library correspondence would be recoverable if the data existed, but the data does not yet exist publicly. This zeroes the data axis on all 27 computational steps.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw sequencing data under a controlled-access study (EGA or dbGaP) or an open accession if consent permits, deposit the processed count matrices and the annotated Seurat/AnnData objects under an open accession or the CZI cell atlas portal, and state the accession, the access route and the expected release date in the preprint rather than deferring to publication.

gaps.where: C9 (Seurat object -> AnnData conversion, on the critical path between C8 and the scVI integration C10)
gaps.missing: 'A custom script was used to convert the Seurat object to Anndata format.' The script is not deposited, not named, not linked and not described. Seurat-to-AnnData conversion is not a neutral operation - which assay, which slot (counts vs data vs scale.data), which metadata columns and which var/obs mapping are carried across determines what scVI is actually trained on. No conversion library (sceasy, zellkonverter, SeuratDisk) is even named, and the anndata citation is an RRID with no version.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the conversion script, or state the conversion package and version plus which assay/slot was exported and which metadata fields were retained.

gaps.where: C19 (SCENIC regulon analysis supporting Figure S5N and the IRF3 / MYF6 / SOX9 regulon claims)
gaps.missing: An entire analysis that produces a supplementary figure and three named biological conclusions appears only in Results ('We performed SCENIC analysis (24) and identified transcriptional networks (regulons) specifically enriched in each fibroblast subset'). There is no Methods paragraph at all: no indication whether pySCENIC, SCENIC (R) or SCENIC+ was run despite the citation being the SCENIC+ paper, no version, no cisTarget/motif ranking database release, no TF list, no number of runs, no AUCell threshold and no regulon specificity score cutoff. The SOX9 regulon enrichment is also used in the Results to support the chondrocyte annotation, so this undocumented step feeds a cell-type claim.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a SCENIC Methods paragraph naming the implementation and version, the motif/cisTarget database release with its download date, the TF list source, the number of independent runs and the regulon/AUCell thresholds, and deposit the resulting regulon table.

gaps.where: C1 (scflow quantnuclei), C9 (anndata), C17 (ggplot2, GO annotation database), C19 (SCENIC), C22 (Xenium Onboard Analysis), C24 (Harmony in the spatial section), C27 (Xenium Explorer)
gaps.missing: Seven invocations carry no version. The orchestration pipeline itself (scflow) is cited as a bare GitHub repository URL with no release, tag or commit - a moving default branch that defines the whole preprocessing chain C1-C3. anndata, ggplot2, the GO/org.Hs.eg.db annotation release behind clusterProfiler, SCENIC, Xenium Onboard Analysis and Xenium Explorer are all named without version numbers, and the Harmony version is stated only in the snRNA-seq section and never restated for the spatial integration. The contrast with the rest of the Methods, where 22 packages are pinned exactly, makes these omissions look like oversights rather than policy - which is why they are worth closing cheaply.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the scflow commit SHA or release tag used, add a software table listing every remaining tool with its exact version including the GO annotation database release and its date, and record the Xenium Onboard Analysis bundle version from the run metadata (it is written into the output directory).

gaps.where: C6 (scDblFinder), C10 (scVI with Ray autotune), C19 (SCENIC), C20 (Liana / CellPhoneDB permutation testing)
gaps.missing: Four stochastic steps report no random seed. scVI is the most consequential: the Ray autotune search space and the hyperparameters it selected are not reported, only that training ran for 60 epochs, so the latent space that every downstream cluster, annotation, MiloR neighbourhood and label transfer depends on cannot be regenerated even with identical inputs and identical package versions. scDblFinder's doublet calls, SCENIC's regulon inference and Liana's permutation p-values are likewise seed-dependent. The best achievable outcome for these steps, even after full artifact release, is distributional agreement rather than exact reproduction.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the random seed (or set.seed / scvi.settings.seed) for every stochastic step, report the autotune search space and the selected scVI hyperparameters explicitly, and deposit the trained scVI model plus the final latent embedding so downstream steps can be reproduced exactly even if the training cannot.

gaps.where: C4 (per-sample QC), C7 (SoupX), C11 (Louvain resolution), C12 (FindAllMarkers), C14 (MiloR), C15 (DESeq2 significance), C17 (clusterProfiler cutoffs), C23 (Xenium filtering), C25 (SCTransform/PCA/UMAP dims), C26 (label transfer)
gaps.missing: The numeric thresholds that determine the cell set, the cluster set and the significance calls are systematically absent even though the package versions are pinned. Specifically: no per-sample cell/feature/mitochondrial cutoffs (C4); SoupX parameters stated to be 'customised to each sample' but not reported (C7); the Louvain resolution chosen after clustree inspection is never given (C11); no test, logFC, min.pct or adjusted-p for FindAllMarkers (C12); no k/d/prop/SpatialFDR for MiloR (C14); no padj or LFC threshold for the DESeq2 LRT (C15); no p/q cutoff and no GO database release for clusterProfiler (C17); 'filtering according to cell size, number of transcripts and number of probes' with no numbers for Xenium (C23); no dims for RunPCA/RunUMAP (C25); no dims, reduction, k.weight or prediction-score cutoff for FindTransferAnchors/TransferData (C26). C13 additionally records a manual step - 'in some cases, smaller clusters were merged' - with no record of which clusters were merged.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a parameters table (or, better, release the scripts, which would close this gap and gap 12 together) giving every threshold per step and per sample, and record the manual cluster-merge decisions as an explicit mapping from pre-merge cluster id to final annotation.

gaps.where: C22 (Xenium Onboard Analysis) and C27 (Xenium Explorer figure generation)
gaps.missing: The first computational step of the spatial half runs on closed 10X Genomics instrument software whose version is not recorded, and the final figure-generation step runs in Xenium Explorer, also unversioned. Cell segmentation - the operation that defines what a 'cell' is in every spatial figure - is described only as 'standard protocols were followed for cell segmentation staining', with no segmentation algorithm, no expansion distance and no nucleus/boundary settings. Onboard Analysis versions differ substantially in segmentation behaviour, so this is not a cosmetic omission.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the Xenium Onboard Analysis version and the segmentation settings from the run's experiment.xenium metadata, and deposit the Onboard Analysis output bundle so downstream reanalysis does not depend on re-running proprietary software.

gaps.where: C19 / W6 (the bespoke 101-gene Xenium Add-On Custom Probe Panel, and Data S1-S3 generally)
gaps.missing: The custom probe panel gene list - which defines what the spatial half can detect and is the reason several snRNA-seq populations (COMPhi THBS4hi fibroblasts, PRG4hi fibroblasts, chondrocytes) could not be confirmed spatially - is deferred entirely to 'Data S3' in the supplementary material, as are Data S1 and Data S2 whose contents are never described in the text. The supplement is referenced only as DC2/DC3/DC4 attachments in the JATS; no format, no accession and no per-file description is given in the manuscript body.
gaps.how_to_close: Describe each supplementary data file in the text (what it contains, which figure it supports), give the probe panel and its design source in a machine-readable format, and deposit the panel design alongside the Xenium data.
